target_customer: Patients in Mexico, especially teens with acne, who pay for video dermatology consultations, prescriptions and skincare products
problem: Mexico has very few dermatologists (the company cites one per 50,000 people), so patients wait long or go untreated.
business_model: Telemedicine consultation fees plus online pharmacy and skincare product sales
product_category: Dermatology telehealth app and online pharmacy for Latin America

founders.name: Saul Armando Lepe Soltero
founders.background_notes: YC page: five years in influencer marketing and an attorney.

technical_complexity.rationale: A video consultation app, e-prescription and pharmacy delivery are standard components; the work was operational (doctor supply, logistics, regulation).

defensibility.rationale: General telemedicine and online pharmacy are easy to copy, and specialist doctors are not exclusive.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; the company site was still selling products in 2026 per a page fetch.

market_need_then: Shortage of dermatologists in Mexico and high teen acne prevalence, as stated by the company on its YC page, plus pandemic-era telemedicine adoption.

identity.visual_style: clean and simple, bold headings, app-focused graphics
identity.voice_and_tone: short, informal Spanish addressing the user as tu

brand_strength.rationale: Spanish-language consumer site with some press (Mexico Business News, 2021) but no evidence of a notable brand asset or community.

outcome_analysis: My NextDerma is listed as active and its website was selling dermatology services and products in 2026, but little independent coverage exists after its 2021 YC batch. Aggregators suggest a very small seed, so it appears to have stayed small and bootstrapped-sized rather than scaling. The cause of limited growth is not public.
notes: Funding: Dealroom, CB Insights and Extruct aggregators give a seed of about 125K to 130K dollars (Y Combinator, Rebel Fund) in early 2021; seen only in aggregators so recorded here as unverified, not as a round. YC page lists three founders; a Forbes Mexico caption reportedly names four (Armando, Luis, Alejandro, Carlos), unopened. Mexico Business News article (April 2021) returned 403 so founder backgrounds and origin were not read. Competitors in Mexico found by search (Miiskin, Doctoralia) came from undated competitor marketing pages, so the list is left empty. No layoffs, shutdown or acquisition found. Completeness pass: CB Insights reports a $0.13M seed on 2021-02-01 (now recorded); Dealroom and Extruct say 125K (Extruct dates it 2021-03). Forbes Mexico reportedly says more than 600K raised, unverified, so the total may be larger than the recorded round. Rests on databases, no press release read.
